answer: Churn is counted in tide, and haven publishes the ratio each epoch. At most 6% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. Someone who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the jetty history. Every extra alias adds 5 hours of verification and 3 percent more locked value. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
